title: synthesis_plan.json
description: A systematic review's pooling model, prespecified at protocol time (PRISMA 2020 item 13a-c) so /litreview-synthesize never selects fixed vs random effects from the data's own heterogeneity statistics. Read by synthesis/run_synthesis.py; written by the review-protocol skill during /litreview-init (or hand-edited for a legacy topic, with retrospective:true).

model.description: The primary pooling model for every poolable outcome in this review. The other model is always computed too and reported under effect_sizes.json's per-outcome "sensitivity" field -- this field only decides which one is primary.

synthesis_family.description: Which synthesis family run_synthesis.py dispatches to (docs/PLAN.md M1/M3; must be one of the resolved method manifest's synthesis.families_allowed -- methods/systematic_review.json allows the first three). "pairwise_iv" is today's inverse-variance pairwise pooling (unchanged default, so a plan predating this field behaves identically). "structured_narrative" never attempts pooling for any outcome, regardless of k. "swim" (Synthesis without Meta-analysis) and "descriptive" (a scoping review's tabulation/charting summary -- docs/PLAN.md M3) are recognized families with no engine yet -- run_synthesis.py refuses cleanly rather than fabricate untested statistics; see synthesis/run_synthesis.py's SWIM_NOT_IMPLEMENTED/DESCRIPTIVE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED messages. In practice a scoping review's protocol never elicits this file at all (review-protocol only writes one when pooling is expected), so "descriptive" here covers a hand-authored plan, not the common path.

tau2_estimator.description: Random-effects between-study variance estimator: "dl" (DerSimonian-Laird, one-step) or "pm" (Paule-Mandel, iterative -- statsmodels' method_re="pm"/"iterated"). Only affects outcomes pooled under model="random"; a fixed-effect pool has no between-study variance to estimate either way.

ci_method.description: Confidence-interval method for the pooled estimate: "normal" (fixed-scale, normal-approximation CI) or "hksj" (modified Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman: an estimated-scale CI using a t-distribution with df=k-1). synthesis/pooling.py flags k<5 under "hksj" as a caution (the correction can be anti-conservative with few studies), but never withholds the estimate.

k_min.description: Minimum number of studies with usable effect data required to pool an outcome group. Raise this above the architectural floor of 2 to require more evidence before trusting a pooled estimate; an outcome group below this threshold falls back to narrative synthesis, same as today's k<2 gate.

identity_fields.description: Fields that must match across studies for their effect estimates to be treated as the same pooling unit (e.g. ["dataset", "acceleration", "metric_definition"] for a benchmark-tabulation review). Schema only in Phase 0 -- the core predicate that refuses pooling across non-identical units arrives later (docs/PLAN.md M5).

pooling_unit.description: Optional; declares what "the same outcome" means for this review beyond the outcome name and measure type. Most clinical reviews omit this.

signed_at.description: When the reviewer signed this plan. Compared against the earliest raw/*.json search-run timestamp to decide whether pooling was actually prespecified (model_source "protocol") or added after study selection (model_source "post_hoc", rendered per PRISMA 2020 item 24c).

justification.description: One or two sentences on why this model (and, if set, this k_min/pooling_unit) was chosen -- not required by the schema, but expected by review-protocol's elicitation.

retrospective.description: Set true only for a legacy topic migrated after search/screening already happened, where signed_at cannot honestly predate the first search run. Suppresses the post_hoc auto-detection; the report must still disclose that pooling was not prespecified.
